text:
Tara Rivera: quick question — onboarding 'orion-13b' from OpenHub. License header says 'NonCommercial + Attribution' and has an extra clause about 'no hosting as a paid service'. Can we include this in the model catalog? Specifically: can we offer embeddings or serve quantized weights to customers? tagging @Matt and @Anya for legal/runtime checks.

Matt Chong (Legal): short answer: NC clauses usually forbid commercial exploitation. If Redwood operates a paid hosted API using the model, that seems like commercial hosting and would violate NC. We need to look at the exact license text; sometimes there are carve-outs for research/academic use. Also "attribution" language may require prominent notices in UI/docs.

Anya Kaur: from the runtime side: quantization itself is fine technically, but "serving quantized weights" to customers (e.g., providing download/export or embedding model binaries in a container) likely counts as redistribution. Serving inference (calls to the model we host) is hosting, not redistribution — still problematic under NC if we charge. If customer runs in Private (their VPC) and brings their own license, that's probably OK.

Liz (license-bot): automated note: detected license -> "OpenHub NC-BY-1.0"; relevant excerpt:
```
"You may not use the Licensed Materials for commercial purposes. Hosting the Licensed Materials as a paid API is prohibited. Attribution required in any public use."
```
Link: https://openhub.example/licenses/nc-by-1.0

Tara Rivera: follow-ups: (1) What about embeddings as a product feature? We return vectors derived from the model to paying customers — is that "use" vs "hosting"? (2) Is Dedicated different from Hosted? Dedicated customers pay us but often have isolated GPU pools managed by Redwood.

Matt Chong (Legal): (1) Embeddings are still output of the model. If you're providing embeddings as a paid feature, that's commercial use. Even if you only store embeddings (and not weights), the license may still restrict that. (2) Dedicated where Redwood controls infra and bills the customer is still a commercial hosting scenario. If the customer self-hosts (Private on-prem or bring-your-own-license) and we only ship orchestration code (no weights), that's safer. We should avoid shipping weights or containers with the model unless licensor grants distribution rights.

Anya Kaur: practical options for product: we can
- Block onboarding into Hosted API catalog (display: "restricted — legal approval required").
- Allow Private deployments if customer supplies proof of license or licensor agreement.
- For Dedicated, require a written attestation + indemnity: customer acknowledges restrictions and obtains necessary rights from licensor.

Tara Rivera: sounds reasonable. Also: for our eval/benchmark runs (internal), is that allowed? We do offline evals to compare quality across models.

Matt Chong (Legal): internal evals for research/non-commercial purposes usually fall under fair use or license allowances, but don't publish benchmark results without attribution and a note about license. If we plan to use results in marketing or to sell the model as part of hosted service, we need explicit permission.

Anya Kaur: one more runtime flag request — can we add a model-catalog tag `usage_restrictions: non-commercial` and an onboarding gate that prevents creation of Hosted endpoints for such models? That would avoid accidental exposure.

Tara Rivera: +1. I'll open a quick PR to the model-catalog with the tag and add a note in the onboarding checklist: "legal sign-off required for NC or other restricted licenses".

Matt Chong (Legal): also recommend we reach out to the model author to ask for a commercial license option; sometimes they're open to dual-licensing. If not, treat as research-only. :thinking:

Liz (license-bot): action items noted: [catalog tag], [legal review], [customer BYOL guidance]. :white_check_mark:

Tara Rivera: thanks all — I'll draft the catalog entry and ping infra to add the onboarding gate.
